# Supported and unavailable features

What a reader might assume exists but does not today.

| Feature | State | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Storage | Preview | Limited/reference workflow. Working-copy runtime not released. |
| Multi-user identity, roles, SSO and MFA | Proposed | The product has one operator account configured through the deployment environment, plus anonymous demo identities. There is no user directory, no roles, no single sign-on, no multi-factor authentication, no password reset and no per-user audit trail. These are proposed, not built. |
| Network-edge protections | Requires operational controls | TLS termination, IP allow-listing, shared rate limiting, request-size limits and restricting operational endpoints are deployment controls. The repository ships example nginx and systemd configuration, which enforces HTTPS, TLS 1.2 or later and a 10 MB body limit but includes no rate limiting. The repository cannot prove how a live deployment is configured. |
| Encryption at rest | Requires operational controls | The application does not encrypt the database, backups or exports itself. Encryption at rest, file permissions and key custody are host or volume controls that must be provided and evidenced by the deployment. |
| Private vulnerability reporting route | Requires operational controls | A private reporting channel has to be enabled and verified by the maintainers. The security policy states that it must not be read as advertising a route that is not yet configured. |
| Independent security assessment | Proposed | No independent penetration test or security audit report is held. Commissioning one, and publishing only its verified outcome, is proposed before institutional use. |
| Incident response and breach notification | Requires operational controls | An incident response plan, on-call ownership and customer notification procedure are operational controls that do not exist in the repository. Legal notification duties also need counsel's input. |
| Production signing key custody | Requires operational controls | The signing seed has to be generated and held in managed key storage by the deployment, its public key committed through review, and rotation exercised. None of that can be proven from the repository. |
| Log retention | Requires operational controls | The application writes logs to standard output. How long they are kept, and who can read them, is decided by the host. An example logrotate file keeps 7 to 14 days. |
| Hosting location and data residency | Requires operational controls | The repository does not fix where a deployment runs. Region, provider and any contractual residency commitment are operational and legal decisions. |
| Data deletion and erasure procedure | Requires operational controls | No product route deletes a project, run or run history. Until one exists, deleting a customer's data is a manual database operation that needs a documented, tested procedure and a legal basis (see known gaps). |
| Backup and restore drill | Requires operational controls | A restore from backup into a clean environment has to be exercised and recorded. |
| Monitoring, alerting, support and service levels | Requires operational controls | Uptime monitoring, alert routing, a support channel and any service-level commitment are operational and contractual matters not present in the repository. |
| Independent security assessment | Proposed | Proposed before institutional use of real client data. |
| Certification roadmap (proposed, not started) | Proposed | No certification programme has been started and none is held. Whether to pursue one is a proposal that has not been decided. |

---
Reviewed 2026-10-10. This pack covers the FINCO Model product: modelling, persistence, authentication, run evidence and release readiness. Radar, Yield and token or wallet features have their own data and controls and are not assessed here. This document describes the product. It is not a legal document, an audit opinion or a certification.
